County Council Report - Mary Lloyd, County Councillor Ward 5
notes: County Councillor Mary Lloyd provided an overview of County Council activities, including the update to the strategic plan, activities at the Wellington County Museum, highlighting the Indigenous Gathering Circle, tree planting, a new art exhibit and the opening of the new children’s playground.
Mayor Watters explained a report will be forthcoming regarding the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing Approval of the Wellington County OPA 119.

items.title: Toni Ellis, Executive Director re Tree Trust
notes: Toni Ellis provided an overview of the work undertaken by Neighbourwoods, in particular, the Tree Trust Program. She explained the Tree Trust Program raises money through donations to hire arborists skilled in conservation arboriculture to preserve legacy trees.

T. Ellis recognized the work the Township has accomplished over the past several years with respect to the importance of trees and offered to work more closely with staff to explore opportunities for remedial work rather than removal, and a foster tree program.
She responded to questions regarding funding sources, and collaboration opportunities.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Councillor MacDonald provided details from the last QMS meeting and outlined recent testing, training and report results.

items.title: Delegations
Ian MacRae spoke in favour of Council adopting a proactive termite
notes: management system aimed at a significant reduction in the termite population. He supports an all encompassing, coordinated, block by block approach to shrink or eradicate the termite population.

Tammy Rutherford expressed support for Option 2 outlined in the staff report, noting homeowners have invested thousands of dollars trying to control termites. She is supportive of undertaking a similar program that the City of Guelph has had success with and a proactive termite management program.

Kirk McElwain spoke in favour of Council adopting a termite management program and noted a product called Sentricon has been approved by Health Canada for use in Canada. He suggested a long-term approach is not necessarily the only option with new technology and chemicals available.

items.title: Consideration of Reports
Health Care Professional Recruitment Update - Phase 1
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer
Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, outlining the stakeholder group’s recommendation for a phased in recruitment approach.

Angela Stanley, President and CEO Wellington Health Care Alliance noted accommodation is the most pressing issue, hosting medical students, residents and physician locums for short periods throughout the year is a crucial tactic for recruiting new medical staff. She indicated finding affordable and stable housing for the short-term medical professionals continues to be challenging.

Dan Wilson indicated the staff recommendation is to use the stone farmhouse on land purchased for the Operations Facility to house healthcare professionals while the operations facility is being designed.

items.title: Termite Management Direction Report
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, including a chronology of events related to termite management over the past several years. D. Wilson outlined the two Options set forth, to either continue with a passive approach to termites or direct staff to release a negotiated request for proposal to initiate a proactive termite management strategy.
D. Wilson responded to questions regarding monies expended to date, encouraging interest in termite management, and proactive enforcement methods.
